title: Relative clauses in a paragraph
subtitle: Use relative clauses to trace the author’s line of thought.
overview: In a paragraph, a relative clause often identifies, characterizes, or advances a previously introduced participant or idea.
Keep its case local to its own clause, but ask why the author attached this clause at this moment.

sections.title: What a relative clause can do

items.grc: ὃ ἦν ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς, ὃ ἀκηκόαμεν, ὃ ἑωράκαμεν.
items.en: What was from the beginning, what we have heard, what we have seen.

items.grc: ὃν ἀπέστειλεν ὁ πατήρ, τοῦτον ὑμεῖς οὐ πιστεύετε.
items.en: The one whom the Father sent, this one you do not believe.
